posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Death isn't a single switch that shuts down your entire body at once. When your heart stops beating and your brain goes silent, trillions of cells inside you are still alive, desperately trying to keep themselves running. Death isn't a single moment, but a slow and surprisingly complex process that can last for weeks.

What actually happens when you die? What makes death so mysterious, and which cells are the last survivors within your body? Watch our full video to find out!

 Daoliao, also known as knife massage, is a traditional practice with roots in ancient Chinese culture, dating back over 2,000 years. ⁠
⁠
Quite an unusual wellness experience to discover in Taiwan!⁠

Sunlight pours through the Sagrada Família's stained-glass windows, filling the interior with glowing shades of blue, green, orange, and red. ⁠
⁠
The cooler tones are on one side and the warmer tones on the other, so the colors change throughout the day as the sun moves across the sky.⁠
⁠
Which photo is more magical? 😍⁠

A beautiful spot to enjoy the water, take in the views and see a different side of the island.⁠
🎥: @everchanginghorizon

⁠

⁠

An underwater Shiva Lingam in Mahakuta, Karnataka, India. 🙏 ⁠
Mahakuta is an important Hindu pilgrimage site, known for its temples dating back to the 6th and 7th centuries, built during the early Chalukya dynasty. ⁠
⁠
A place where history, architecture and faith come together.⁠
🎥: @aakansha_diary

Stranger Things: The Diner is a limited-time immersive dining experience inspired by the hit Netflix series. Over 90 minutes, guests can eat, drink, and explore scenes from all five seasons, with a themed menu, photo ops, and official merchandise along the way.⁠
⁠
The diner runs from November 18 to February 28 at The Matriarch on W 42nd Street, with tickets starting at around $30 per person.⁠
⁠
Who would you bring with you to Hawkins? ⁠
⁠
By: @strangerthingsdiner

Ever tried a toboggan ride this long? 🛷🇿🇦 ⁠
This one near Sabie is said to be the longest in Africa, and it looks like so much fun!⁠
🎥: @jess_eras

This adorable bear in Svalbard was playing with a drifting log, and it looks like it's giving a high-five!⁠
⁠
A polar bear's paws can measure up to 12 inches across. Small bumps on the pads help them grip the ice; fur between the toes keeps them from slipping, and when swimming, the front paws do almost all of the work. 🐾⁠
⁠
Which photo is the cutest?⁠
⁠
By: @jackjeffress

Popcorn, Nepalese style! 🍿🔥 ⁠
⁠
Made the traditional way using a coal pit and a basket filled with kernels. Such a simple but fascinating way to make everyone's favourite snack!⁠
🎥: @sociallywanderful

Two centuries ago, French inventor Nicéphore Niépce took what may be the earliest surviving photograph with a camera obscura. While he may not have captured any people or animals, his image showcased a moment in time. Today, photos are more accessible than ever, but the most fascinating images continue to live in a particular time and place, constantly altering our sense of who we are and highlighting moments that many of us may not otherwise see.
